Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians

This is a separate current community route; it is not an alias automatically applied to every historical Grand River band or another present Ottawa government.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

A community account of place and purpose

The Band’s Our story describes 19 historical Ottawa bands living along the Grand River and other southwest Michigan waterways. Read alongside it, the Mission Statement emphasizes preserving culture and traditions and educating members and the public. This is the contemporary community’s own account; its name should not be applied automatically to every historical Grand River band or another Ottawa government.

Read the sources [1] Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians

02

A documented public-history partnership

In its 2021 Community Engagement Report, the Grand Rapids Public Museum records working with the Grand River Bands and Downtown Grand Rapids Inc. on an event commemorating the 1821 Treaty of Chicago. This supplies a dated example of the community participating in how regional history is presented. The report describes the event rather than resolving the treaty’s later interpretation.

Read the sources [2] Grand Rapids Public Museum

Community Engagement Report 2021 —1821 Treaty Commemoration ↗

Publication: 2021

The Museum records a specific partnership with the Grand River Bands and Downtown Grand Rapids Inc. This dated example makes a useful companion to the Band’s own account.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Physical PDF page 7, printed page 5, entire 1821 Treaty Commemoration paragraph read in extracted text and rendered page image. Nearby sections were inspected for context; their statistics are not applied to the Bands. The original 1821 treaty, event recording, participant views and other report pages were not substantively reviewed.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
